name: Sirocco Vigil
specific_features: Automated beacon broadcasting a decades-old distress loop
Abandoned research outpost on the canyon rim
description: Sirocco Vigil is a rust-orange world of endless dune seas broken by canyon systems so deep their floors never see direct sunlight. Its wispy atmosphere does little to soften the light, which falls harsh and white across wind-carved spires of sandstone. By day the surface bakes under its pale sun; by night the temperature collapses, and frost glitters on the canyon rims.

There is almost no sound here beyond the whisper of grit against grit, a hiss that never quite stops. The air carries the dry mineral smell of crushed rock and something faintly organic rising from the canyon depths. At dusk the sky burns violet, and the dropping cold makes the whole world creak and settle like an old ship.

Survey teams found microbial mats clinging to seep water deep in the canyons, the last remnants of a biosphere that once may have been richer. On the canyon rim stands an abandoned research outpost, its instruments still pointed downward at the colonies it was built to protect. Beside it, an automated beacon has repeated the same distress call for over thirty years, though every recorded crew member was accounted for when the station was evacuated.

Corporations covet the planet's silicon fields and its position along a busy shipping lane, while xenobiologists warn that the canyon ecosystems are one drought from extinction. Whoever claims the outpost will inherit its data cores, its unanswered questions, and the mystery of who triggered that beacon. The vigil, it seems, is still being kept by someone.
